text_blocks.snippet: U.S. citizens do not need a visa to enter Greece for stays of up to 90 days for tourism or business purposes. However, they will need a Schengen visa for longer stays or for purposes other than tourism or business, such as for work or study. Additionally, U.S. citizens traveling on official or diplomatic passports must obtain a Schengen visa prior to arrival, regardless of the length of stay.

list.title: Official/Diplomatic Passports:

list.title: Residence Permits:

Starting in the last quarter of 2026, U.S. citizens will need to obtain ETIAS authorization (European Travel Information and Authorization System) before traveling to Greece and other Schengen countries for short stays.
ETIAS is an online application process and is expected to be a relatively simple procedure.
Denial of Entry: Greek immigration authorities can deny entry even if a U.S. citizen has a valid passport and meets the visa requirements.
Passport Validity: Always check your passport's expiration date well in advance of your trip.
Official Travel: If traveling on official or diplomatic passports, ensure you have the necessary visa or authorization before departure.
